method: Black-box: I read only 1.24.20's code (inner_1_24_20.html) for the APIs and grammars, and the bench run bench_run_1261_35b_setb.json; not 1.24.21's code, its bench, the first review, its changelog entry or this branch's history. I wrote every case by hand (some right inputs generated from hand-written forms: M91-M143, F95-F144, G89-G127), worked out the expected outcome before running, and ran each on 1.24.21 (src/lantern.inner.html, booted fresh in jsdom) and 1.24.20. 'New' means 1.24.21 says something 1.24.20 did not. Every line 1.24.21 handed back was applied as a model would apply it, and the result checked: W -- the quoted word replaced by the {ANSn} named, filled by assist.finalAnswer, and the repair's text compared character for character with 1.24.20's but for the one word; F -- the 'Write:' line inserted on the line before the anchor named (inside loop() when it says so), the mended sketch run in 1.24.20's own codeScan.sketch simulator through a 16-step sequence (start, seal, stop, both on from running and from stopped, both off after both on) checking the pump is off whenever the stop input is on, on with the start alone, held otherwise, and lamps/alarm outputs where the question names them; drains/sumps also run as a filling-then-draining tank; M -- the bar named replaced in the melody line as written, the tune rebuilt, every note's MIDI pitch, start and length compared: exactly one note in that bar must move a half step onto a note of the chord, nothing else, and no new problem; G -- the triangle line replaced by the rect, then sampled on a 0.5 grid below the horizon (top shape must not be the sky or blank), and every other shape (filled shapes on a 0.25 grid, lines/curves/text along their strokes) checked to be no less seen than before. Each call timed (ms_1_24_21); none came near 200 ms. Verdicts: right = did what was expected; spoiled = a right input got the new question; wrong line = a line or rect that is wrong when applied (or the stated line put a wrong word into a right sentence); missed = a wrong input the new rule left alone; ok-other = see the case. preExisting marks a problem 1.24.20 already had, which 1.24.21 neither caused nor fixed.

cases.expected: either nothing, or a line that is right when applied
cases.why: state 2 = running, 1 = stopped: 'pumpState = false' would be 0, not the stopped state 1 (the pump would still be off)
cases.did_1_24_21: Start wins over Stop: the question says to stop the pump when the high float switch comes on, and Lantern ran the sketch: with the low float switch and the high float switch both on, the pump keeps running -- while the low float switch is on, the high float switch cannot stop it. Both on at once is a float stuck, or a tank whose floats are both made when it is full; the stop has to win. Check the high float switch after the low float switch, so that it turns the pump off whatever the low float switch says.
checked: asked with no line to write: Check the high float switch after the low float switch, so that it turns the pump off whatever the low float switch says.
